verses.original: Λέγω δέ ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ὁ κληρονόμος νήπιός ἐστιν οὐδὲν διαφέρει δούλου κύριος πάντων ὤν
verses.transliteration: Legō de eph’ hoson chronon ho klēronomos nēpios estin ouden diapherei doulou kyrios pantōn ōn
verses.literal: What I am saying is that as long as . . . . . . the heir is a child he is no different . . . from a slave although he is the owner of everything
verses.literalPt: DIGO, pois, que todo o tempo que o herdeiro é menino em nada difere do servo, ainda que seja senhor de tudo;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ ἐπιτρόπους ἐστὶν καὶ οἰκονόμους ἄχρι τῆς προθεσμίας τοῦ πατρός
verses.transliteration: alla hypo epitropous estin kai oikonomous achri tēs prothesmias tou patros
verses.literal: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father
verses.literalPt: Mas está debaixo de tutores e curadores até ao tempo determinado pelo pai.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ὅτε ἦμεν νήπιοι ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ἤμεθα δεδουλωμένοι
verses.transliteration: houtōs kai hēmeis hote ēmen nēpioi hypo ta stoicheia tou kosmou ēmetha dedoulōmenoi
verses.literal: So also when we were children we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world
verses.literalPt: Assim também nós, quando éramos meninos, estávamos reduzidos à servidão debaixo dos primeiros rudimentos do mundo.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός γενόμενον ὑπὸ νόμον
verses.transliteration: Hote de ēlthen to plērōma tou chronou exapesteilen ho Theos ton Huion autou genomenon ek gynaikos genomenon hypo nomon
verses.literal: But when the time had fully come God sent His Son born of a woman born under the law
verses.literalPt: Mas, vindo a plenitude dos tempos, Deus enviou seu Filho, nascido de mulher, nascido sob a lei,

verses.original: ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ ἵνα τὴν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν
verses.transliteration: hina tous hypo nomon exagorasē hina tēn huiothesian apolabōmen
verses.literal: to redeem those under the law that we might receive our adoption as sons
verses.literalPt: Para remir os que estavam debaixo da lei, a fim de recebermos a adoção de filhos.

verses.original: Ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν κρᾶζον Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ
verses.transliteration: Hoti de este huioi exapesteilen ho Theos to Pneuma tou Huiou autou eis tas kardias hēmōn krazon Abba ho Patēr
verses.literal: And because you are sons God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts crying out Abba Father
verses.literalPt: E, porque sois filhos, Deus enviou aos vossos corações o Espírito de seu Filho, que clama: Aba, Pai.

verses.original: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος ἀλλὰ υἱός εἰ δὲ υἱός καὶ κληρονόμος διὰ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: hōste ouketi ei doulos alla huios ei de huios kai klēronomos dia Theou
verses.literal: So you are no longer a slave but a son and since you are a son you are also an heir through God
verses.literalPt: Assim que já não és mais servo, mas filho; e, se és filho, és também herdeiro de Deus por Cristo.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες Θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς φύσει μὴ οὖσιν θεοῖς
verses.transliteration: Alla tote men ouk eidotes Theon edouleusate tois physei mē ousin theois
verses.literal: Formerly when you did not know God you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods
verses.literalPt: Mas, quando não conhecíeis a Deus, servíeis aos que por natureza não são deuses.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ γνόντες Θεόν μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ Θεοῦ πῶς ἐπιστρέφετε πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ καὶ πτωχὰ στοιχεῖα οἷς πάλιν ἄνωθεν δουλεύειν θέλετε
verses.transliteration: nyn de gnontes Theon mallon de gnōsthentes hypo Theou pōs epistrephete palin epi ta asthenē kai ptōcha stoicheia hois palin anōthen douleuein thelete
verses.literal: But now that you know God or rather are known by God how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again
verses.literalPt: Mas agora, conhecendo a Deus, ou, antes, sendo conhecidos por Deus, como tornais outra vez a esses rudimentos fracos e pobres, aos quais de novo quereis servir?

verses.original: ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτούς
verses.transliteration: hēmeras paratēreisthe kai mēnas kai kairous kai eniautous
verses.literal: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years
verses.literalPt: Guardais dias, e meses, e tempos, e anos.

verses.original: φοβοῦμαι ὑμᾶς μή πως εἰκῇ κεκοπίακα εἰς ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: phoboumai hymas mē pōs eikē kekopiaka eis hymas
verses.literal: I fear for you that my efforts for you may have been in vain
verses.literalPt: Receio de vós, que não haja trabalhado em vão para convosco.

verses.original: Γίνεσθε ὡς ἐγώ ὅτι κἀγὼ ὡς ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί δέομαι ὑμῶν οὐδέν με ἠδικήσατε
verses.transliteration: Ginesthe hōs egō hoti kagō hōs hymeis adelphoi deomai hymōn ouden me ēdikēsate
verses.literal: I beg you brothers become like me for I became like you You have done me no wrong . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Irmãos, rogo-vos que sejais como eu, porque também eu sou como vós; nenhum mal me fizestes.

verses.original: Οἴδατε δὲ ὅτι δι’ ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν τὸ πρότερον
verses.transliteration: Oidate de hoti di’ astheneian tēs sarkos euēngelisamēn hymin to proteron
verses.literal: You know that it was because of an illness . . . . . . that I first preached the gospel . . . . . . to you
verses.literalPt: E vós sabeis que primeiro vos anunciei o evangelho estando em fraqueza da carne;

verses.original: καὶ τὸν πειρασμὸν ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου οὐκ ἐξουθενήσατε οὐδὲ ἐξεπτύσατε ἀλλὰ ὡς ἄγγελον Θεοῦ ἐδέξασθέ με ὡς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: kai ton peirasmon hymōn en tē sarki mou ouk exouthenēsate oude exeptysate alla hōs angelon Theou edexasthe me hōs Christon Iēsoun
verses.literal: And although my illness was a trial to you you did not despise or reject me Instead you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God as if I were Christ Jesus Himself
verses.literalPt: E não rejeitastes, nem desprezastes isso que era uma tentação na minha carne, antes me recebestes como um anjo de Deus, como Jesus Cristo mesmo.

verses.original: ποῦ οὖν ὁ μακαρισμὸς ὑμῶν μαρτυρῶ γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν ἐξορύξαντες ἐδώκατέ μοι
verses.transliteration: pou oun ho makarismos hymōn martyrō gar hymin hoti ei dynaton tous ophthalmous hymōn exoryxantes edōkate moi
verses.literal: What then has become of your blessing For I can testify that if it were possible you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me
verses.literalPt: Qual é, logo, a vossa bem-aventurança? Porque vos dou testemunho de que, se possível fora, arrancaríeis os vossos olhos, e mos daríeis.

verses.original: ὥστε ἐχθρὸς ὑμῶν γέγονα ἀληθεύων ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: hōste echthros hymōn gegona alētheuōn hymin
verses.literal: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth . . .
verses.literalPt: Fiz-me acaso vosso inimigo, dizendo a verdade?

verses.original: Ζηλοῦσιν ὑμᾶς οὐ καλῶς ἀλλὰ ἐκκλεῖσαι ὑμᾶς θέλουσιν ἵνα αὐτοὺς ζηλοῦτε
verses.transliteration: Zēlousin hymas ou kalōs alla ekkleisai hymas thelousin hina autous zēloute
verses.literal: Those people are zealous for you . . . but not in a good way Instead they want to isolate you from us so that you may be zealous for them
verses.literalPt: Eles têm zelo por vós, não como convém; mas querem excluir-vos, para que vós tenhais zelo por eles.

verses.original: καλὸν δὲ ζηλοῦσθαι ἐν καλῷ πάντοτε καὶ μὴ μόνον ἐν τῷ παρεῖναί με πρὸς ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: kalon de zēlousthai en kalō pantote kai mē monon en tō pareinai me pros hymas
verses.literal: Nevertheless it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose at any time and not only when I am with you
verses.literalPt: É bom ser zeloso, mas sempre do bem, e não somente quando estou presente convosco.

verses.original: Τέκνα μου οὓς πάλιν ὠδίνω μέχρις οὗ μορφωθῇ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Tekna mou hous palin ōdinō mechris hou morphōthē Christos en hymin
verses.literal: My children for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you
verses.literalPt: Meus filhinhos, por quem de novo sinto as dores de parto, até que Cristo seja formado em vós;

verses.original: ἤθελον δὲ παρεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄρτι καὶ ἀλλάξαι τὴν φωνήν μου ὅτι ἀποροῦμαι ἐν ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: ēthelon de pareinai pros hymas arti kai allaxai tēn phōnēn mou hoti aporoumai en hymin
verses.literal: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone because I am perplexed about you
verses.literalPt: Eu bem quisera agora estar presente convosco, e mudar a minha voz; porque estou perplexo a vosso respeito.

verses.original: Λέγετέ μοι οἱ ὑπὸ νόμον θέλοντες εἶναι τὸν νόμον οὐκ ἀκούετε
verses.transliteration: Legete moi hoi hypo nomon thelontes einai ton nomon ouk akouete
verses.literal: Tell me you who want to be under the law do you not understand what the law says
verses.literalPt: Dizei-me, os que quereis estar debaixo da lei, não ouvis vós a lei?

verses.original: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἀβραὰμ δύο υἱοὺς ἔσχεν ἕνα ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας
verses.transliteration: gegraptai gar hoti Abraam dyo huious eschen hena ek tēs paidiskēs kai hena ek tēs eleutheras
verses.literal: For it is written that Abraham had two sons one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman
verses.literalPt: Porque está escrito que Abraão teve dois filhos, um da escrava, e outro da livre.

verses.original: ἀλλ’ ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται ὁ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας δι’ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας
verses.transliteration: all’ ho men ek tēs paidiskēs kata sarka gegennētai ho de ek tēs eleutheras di’ tēs epangelias
verses.literal: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh but his son by the free woman was born through the promise
verses.literalPt: Todavia, o que era da escrava nasceu segundo a carne, mas, o que era da livre, por promessa.

verses.original: ἅτινά ἐστιν ἀλληγορούμενα αὗται γάρ εἰσιν δύο διαθῆκαι μία μὲν ἀπὸ ὄρους Σινᾶ εἰς δουλείαν γεννῶσα ἥτις ἐστὶν Ἁγάρ
verses.transliteration: hatina estin allēgoroumena hautai gar eisin dyo diathēkai mia men apo orous Sina eis douleian gennōsa hētis estin Hagar
verses.literal: These things serve as illustrations for the women represent two covenants One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery This is Hagar
verses.literalPt: O que se entende por alegoria; porque estas são as duas alianças; uma, do monte Sinai, gerando filhos para a servidão, que é Agar.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ Ἁγὰρ Σινᾶ ὄρος ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ Ἀραβίᾳ συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἰερουσαλήμ δουλεύει γὰρ μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: to de Hagar Sina oros estin en tē Arabia systoichei de tē nyn Ierousalēm douleuei gar meta tōn teknōn autēs
verses.literal: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem because she is in slavery with her children
verses.literalPt: Ora, esta Agar é Sinai, um monte da Arábia, que corresponde à Jerusalém que agora existe, pois é escrava com seus filhos.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ἄνω Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐλευθέρα ἐστίν ἥτις ἐστὶν μήτηρ ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: hē de anō Ierousalēm eleuthera estin hētis estin mētēr hēmōn
verses.literal: But the Jerusalem above is free and she is our mother
verses.literalPt: Mas a Jerusalém que é de cima é livre; a qual é mãe de todos nós.

verses.original: γέγραπται γάρ Εὐφράνθητι στεῖρα ἡ οὐ τίκτουσα ῥῆξον καὶ βόησον ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα
verses.transliteration: gegraptai gar Euphranthēti steira hē ou tiktousa rhēxon kai boēson hē ouk ōdinousa hoti polla ta tekna tēs erēmou mallon ē tēs echousēs ton andra
verses.literal: For it is written Rejoice O barren woman who bears no children break forth and cry aloud you who have never travailed because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband
verses.literalPt: Porque está escrito: Alegra-te, estéril, que não dás à luz; Esforça-te e clama, tu que não estás de parto; Porque os filhos da solitária são mais do que os da que tem marido.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀδελφοί κατὰ Ἰσαὰκ ἐπαγγελίας τέκνα ἐστέ
verses.transliteration: Hymeis de adelphoi kata Isaak epangelias tekna este
verses.literal: Now you brothers like Isaac are children of promise
verses.literalPt: Mas nós, irmãos, somos filhos da promessa como Isaque.

verses.original: ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ τότε ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐδίωκεν τὸν κατὰ Πνεῦμα οὕτως καὶ νῦν
verses.transliteration: all’ hōsper tote ho kata sarka gennētheis ediōken ton kata Pneuma houtōs kai nyn
verses.literal: At that time however the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit It is the same . . . now
verses.literalPt: Mas, como então aquele que era gerado segundo a carne perseguia o que o era segundo o Espírito, assim é também agora.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς οὐ γὰρ μὴ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἐλευθέρας
verses.transliteration: Alla ti legei hē graphē Ekbale tēn paidiskēn kai ton huion autēs ou gar mē klēronomēsei ho huios tēs paidiskēs meta tou huiou tēs eleutheras
verses.literal: But what does the Scripture say Expel the slave woman and her son for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son
verses.literalPt: Mas que diz a Escritura? Lança fora a escrava e seu filho, porque de modo algum o filho da escrava herdará com o filho da livre.

verses.original: διό ἀδελφοί οὐκ ἐσμὲν παιδίσκης τέκνα ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐλευθέρας
verses.transliteration: dio adelphoi ouk esmen paidiskēs tekna alla tēs eleutheras
verses.literal: Therefore brothers we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman
verses.literalPt: De maneira que, irmãos, somos filhos, não da escrava, mas da livre.
